Playbook.name: AD — Kerberos Replay Attack Detected - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: Windows raised 4649 ('a replay attack was detected') - the KDC saw a duplicated authenticator. Triage question: genuine ticket replay, or the well-known benign cause (clock/duplicate request quirks, load balancers re-sending)?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Real Kerberos replay implies an attacker on the network path reusing captured authenticators - rare but severe.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

Input.name: $target_user
Input.description: Account named in the 4649 event (from INV-01).

InitialAssessment.Rule: 4649 in isolation with no other auth anomalies for the involved principal is usually a protocol quirk; verify before closing.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the 4649 is an isolated protocol artifact or coincides with real duplicated-authentication behavior for the same principal.

Step.name: Pull the 4649 events and involved principals
Step.Purpose: Get the exact principals/hosts involved - 4649 is rare, every instance matters.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4649" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, host.name, winlog.event_data.TargetUserName, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.computer_name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: Note the involved account(s). Several 4649s for different accounts on one DC in a short span leans infrastructure quirk; repeated 4649 for ONE account is more suspicious.

Step.name: Involved account's authentication picture around the event
Step.Purpose: Real replay should coincide with duplicate/parallel session behavior for the account: same-second logons from different sources.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("4624","4625","4771","4768") AND winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code) BY src | SORT c DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: Two different sources authenticating as the same account in the same window supports replay/credential sharing; a single source points to client retry quirks.

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows the same account authenticating from two or more distinct sources in the same window, corroborating duplicated authenticators.
Node.Result: True Positive (Possible Replay - escalate to IR)

Node.Condition: Single 4649 with no duplicated-source behavior and a known time-skew/load-balancer path involved.
4649s recur on one DC across many accounts (KDC-side quirk, patch level or NLB re-send).
Account context is incomplete (no source data) - cannot corroborate either way.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-REPLAY-EVENTS, INV-02-REPLAY-CONTEXT to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Protocol/infrastructure artifact (retransmission, clock skew) without any duplicated-session evidence.

Indicators.Item: No dual-source authentication for the account.

SOCAction.Item: Document and close as false_positive; monitor recurrence.

TruePositive.Definition: An on-path actor replayed captured Kerberos material.

Indicators.Item: Dual-source simultaneous authentication for the account.
Follow-on access from the second source.

SOCAction.Item: Reset the account and revoke tickets.
Investigate the network path for interception; escalate to IR.

Misconfiguration.Definition: Systemic KDC/infrastructure behavior repeatedly producing 4649 without malicious cause.

Indicators.Item: Recurring across accounts on the same DC.
Correlates with NLB retransmits or clock drift (0x25 skew also elevated).

SOCAction.Item: Engage AD platform team: fix time sync / NLB behavior; document the pattern.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Identify involved account and freeze if dual-source is confirmed.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Reset credentials; inspect network path segment for capture points.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Time-sync hygiene; review NLB Kerberos handling.

QualityChecks.Check: 4649 volume in JCB 90d was near zero - any burst is itself signal.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Account reset; path investigated; findings recorded.
